subject: POC: technical onboarding workshop — slot realignment & load-test dry run
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily@atlasretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff & hands-on workshop — proposed slots and agenda

Hi Emily —

Great to be moving forward with Atlas Retail's POC. I wanted to propose a concrete plan so we can lock calendar slots this week. Goal is a two-part engagement:

1) POC kickoff (60 min) — align goals, scope, success criteria, and test data
2) Hands-on workshop (3 hrs) — prompt review, routing checks, and a controlled load-testing window (throughput and latency verification)

High-level proposed agenda attached (proposed-agenda-v1.pdf) and a short test-harness overview (test-harness-overview.md). Can you confirm which of these options work for your team (PST times shown):

• Tue 25 May — 10:00–14:00 (kickoff + hands-on same day)
• Wed 26 May — Kickoff 09:00–10:00, hands-on 13:00–16:00
• Thu 27 May — Kickoff 14:00–15:00, hands-on 15:30–18:30

Couple of quick asks so we size the load test correctly:
- Expected steady-state concurrency (requests/sec) and peak burst profile
- Typical sequence lengths (tokens) for the core flows you want validated
- A list of people who should join the hands-on (DevOps, App owners, and one product decision-maker)

If none of those slots work, suggest two windows and we’ll adapt. We’d also like to run a 30–60 minute dry-run with your DevOps the day before the hands-on to validate network egress and the test harness.

Thanks — I’ll hold the first two options tentatively.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: proposed-agenda-v1.pdf, test-harness-overview.md
From: Emily Tran <emily@atlasretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: devops@atlasretail.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & hands-on workshop — proposed slots and agenda

Hi Jordan —

Thanks, the plan looks good. A couple of notes from our side:

• The team prefers afternoon slots — Wed 26 May for kickoff in the morning is a bit tight for our leadership. Thu 27 May (kickoff 14:00) + hands-on same afternoon works best.
• Throughput target: our baseline is ~120 TPS for search-like prompts, bursts up to 300 TPS for 30–60s. Typical prompt sequences average ~90 tokens, but some recommendation flows go to ~350 tokens.
• Attendees: Me (Product), Aman Khurana (devops@atlasretail.com), Priya Singh (engineering manager), and Sara Lopez (app owner) — I’ll forward invites once times are confirmed.

One more ask: can Redwood run the dry-run with Aman on Wed 26 May, afternoon? He prefers a short window 15:00–16:00 PST to test connectivity.

Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Product, Atlas Retail
emily@atlasretail.com | +1 (206) 555-0147
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC kickoff & hands-on workshop — proposed slots and agenda

Jordan / Monica —

Thanks for the notes. We can support Thu 27 May as Emily requested. Operational checklist below for the hands-on and the dry-run:

Dry-run (Wed 26 May, 15:00–16:00 PST)
- Verify VPN / VPC egress rules to Redwood endpoints
- Validate test-harness auth token and sample payloads
- Quick smoke of routing policies and model selection (we'll use r-infer-2.3 quantized and r-infer-2.3-fp16 as fallbacks)

Hands-on (Thu 27 May, 14:00–17:30 PST)
- 14:00 – 14:30 Kickoff: success metrics and data handling
- 14:30 – 15:30 Prompt review & routing verification
- 15:30 – 17:00 Controlled load test (we'll do stepped increases: 50, 120, 200, 300 TPS; hold each step 2–5 minutes)
- 17:00 – 17:30 Results walk and next steps

We should run the dry-run with BenchLab's harness if Atlas wants a reproducible runbook — I'll loop benchmarks@loadlab.io if needed. I attached a short runbook checklist for the dry-run (runbook-dryrun-checklist.pdf).

Also: Monica, can you confirm GPU pool availability (we prefer to reserve 2 x A100 equivalent for the load window)? If not available, we can adjust the stepped plan.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: runbook-dryrun-checklist.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & hands-on workshop — slot realignment & load-test dry run

Emily / Aman —

Thanks for the quick replies. Thu 27 May is confirmed on our side. I sent calendar invites for both sessions (Dry-run: Wed 26 May 15:00–16:00 PST; Hands-on: Thu 27 May 14:00–17:30 PST). Links are in the invite (https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123). Please accept when convenient.

Pre-session deliverables from Atlas (please upload to the Drive folder ahead of Wed's dry-run):
- Sample payloads and representative traffic profile (CSV or JSON)
- Short list of priority prompt templates (ideally converted to our prompt review sheet)
- Any IP/network allowlist CIDRs for egress testing (Aman)

We’ll provide: runbook checklist, the harness endpoint, and a small repo with sample payloads (we'll post to the Drive folder linked below).

If anything changes on timing I’ll notify the group; otherwise we’ll treat the dry-run as mandatory to avoid surprises during the hands-on.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake

jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
